messages:
liz_support: Hey team, just got a ticket from AcmeCorp — their p99 for /v1/stream is spiking to ~3.2s since ~10:15 UTC, started after a deploy. Customer says most requests are tiny prompts. No errors reported, just latency + occasional 504s. Can someone triage? :grimacing:
trent_eng: looking. do we have sample request ids? liz_support: forwarded logs: trace=tx_9f3b, tx_9f3c, tx_9f3d. headers show tenant_id=acme-prod, model=gpt-redwood-3.
maria_sre: pulling traces now. sending initial p95/p99 from metrics: baseline p99 ~900ms, now ~3200ms. spike correlates with increased small-prompt traffic (<=12 tokens) starting at 10:14:50.
trent_eng: small prompts -> continuous batcher edge case maybe. any config changes in last deploy? ben_infra: we rolled batching defaults in cfg v2.8.3 at 10:12 UTC — lowered min_batch_size from 8->4 and kept linger_ms=15. that reduces latency normally but might change coalescing behavior for microbursts.
liz_support: customer says they ramped a burst of tiny requests as part of a canary, could be that.
maria_sre: repro note: when many tiny requests hit, continuous-batcher can form tiny batches that extend KV cache lifetime and cause head-of-line blocking behind a request stuck waiting for hold window. when concurrency is low, a single long-wait batch holds GPU and delays others -> p99 explosion.
trent_eng: getting a stack of hung slices in the batcher logs: ```
2026-03-15T10:15:03Z batcher: hold_start id=0x7fa3 wait_for_size=4 linger_ms=15 requests=2
2026-03-15T10:15:04Z batcher: dispatch_batch id=0x7fa3 size=2 duration_ms=1100
2026-03-15T10:15:05Z batcher: batch_pending id=0x3b9a waiting_for_prefix_cache
```
maria_sre: also seeing a pattern: requests with small prompts + function-calling metadata are taking ~1.1s in the runtime due to extra serialization but batcher still waits for size threshold, creating interleaving delays.
ben_infra: also noticed tenant-specific rate limiter tripping and queuing requests on the same executor — that exacerbates head-of-line blocking. single tenant with bursty tiny requests can monopolize a GPU slot.
liz_support: customer wants mitigation asap — what's the quick fix?
trent_eng: short term options: 1) roll back cfg v2.8.3 to previous batching defaults (increase min_batch_size back to 8) OR 2) reduce linger_ms to 0-2ms for affected fleet so smaller hold window. Both require deploy/rollout.
maria_sre: third option: enable per-tenant concurrency isolation (quick patch: route acme-prod to a different executor pool or increase their pool size) — takes a bit more orchestration but minimal code change.
ben_infra: I can patch routing flag for acme-prod to tenant_pool=burst-protected in the control plane and scale that pool by +2 GPUs. ready to push if SRE + product ok.
trent_eng: for immediate mitigation, set linger_ms=2 on the canary nodes (fast rollout). I'll prepare a hotpatch: `cfg.batch.linger_ms=2` and a rollout to 10% -> 100% in 10m.
liz_support: pls go ahead. i'll tell customer we're applying an immediate config adjustment and ask them to pause their canary for 30m.
ops-bot: Deploy started by trent_eng: batch-config-hotpatch -> targets: batcher-fleet-canary -> change: linger_ms 15->2. link: https://ops/deploy/98765
trent_eng: hotpatch completed on canary nodes. monitoring...
maria_sre: metrics trending: p99 on canary nodes dropped to ~950ms within 30s. global p99 still high because other nodes haven't moved.
ben_infra: routing flag for acme-prod applied to burst-protected pool and scaled (+2 GPUs). that should prevent tenant headlock while we roll fleet change.
liz_support: customer confirms latency dropped to ~1.0s after we scaled them and reduced linger. they will continue tests. thanks. :relieved:
trent_eng: long-term: we should add a small-prompt fast-path: if request.token_count <= 16 and function_call metadata small, bypass wait-for-size and use immediate dispatch on reserved micro-batcher. also add tenant isolation heuristics and a safeguard that prevents more than N concurrent batches from the same tenant on a single executor.
maria_sre: agree. also add a telemetry event when batch wait duration > X ms and batch size < Y so we can auto-detect headlock patterns.
ben_infra: created an infra ticket INFRA-5921 for pool isolation automation and marked high priority.
liz_support: I'll keep the support ticket open until customer closes. next steps: trent to schedule rollout of linger_ms change to the rest of fleet after smoke tests; ben to automate tenant routing; maria to add telemetry alert; support to confirm customer tests pass.
trent_eng: scheduling rollout for 10:40 UTC. will post progress.
liz_support: thanks all. adding notes to the support ticket with repro steps we used: curl example below for reproducing tiny burst locally:
```bash
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream \\  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TOKEN" \\  -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme-prod" \\  -d '{"model":"gpt-redwood-3","input":"hi","max_tokens":8}' &
done; wait
```
liz_support: I'll attach the logs (tx_9f3b..tx_9f3d) to the ticket. closing here once full rollout is done. :white_check_mark:
